how-are-you.note: Swedes say du, you, to everyone

please.note: Swedish has no everyday please: put tack at the end of a request, En kaffe, tack (a coffee, thanks)

thank-you.note: Tack så mycket (tak so MÜ-keh) means thank you very much

youre-welcome.note: Literally "no reason". Varsågod (VAR-sho-good) means here you are

yes.note: Swedes also say yes with a quick intake of breath

no.note: Nej tack is no, thank you

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention or get past

my-name.note: The audio uses Peter as the example name

lets-go.note: Literally "now we drive", said for any start

speak-english.note: Nearly every Swede speaks excellent English, but a few words of Swedish are always appreciated

thousand.note: Prices are in kronor (KROO-nor), written kr or SEK

would-like.note: The polite way to order. Simpler still: just the thing and tack. The audio uses en kaffe (en KAF-feh), a coffee
would-like.spoken: Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe

i-want.note: Literally "I'll take...", the natural way in a shop. The audio uses den här (den hair), this one

do-you-have.note: Ni (nee) is "you all", the usual way to ask a shop. The audio uses vatten (VAT-en), water

discount.note: Prices are fixed; bargaining only at flea markets (loppis)

card.note: Sweden is nearly cashless: many places take only cards or phones

toilet.note: Var (vaar) means where. Public toilets often need a card or phone payment

taxi.text: Kan du ringa efter en taxi?
taxi.say: kan dü RING-a EF-ter en TAK-see
taxi.note: Check the price sticker on the window before you get in

train-station.note: The main station in a city is the centralstation

which-train.note: The audio uses Göteborg (yö-teh-BOR-y), Gothenburg, as the example

buy-ticket.text: Var kan jag köpa en biljett?
buy-ticket.say: vaar kan yaa SHÖ-pa en bil-YET
buy-ticket.note: Tickets are mostly bought in the SJ app

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Göteborg as the example

trip-length.text: Hur lång tid tar det till...?
trip-length.say: hür long teed taar deh til ...
trip-length.note: The audio uses Göteborg as the example
trip-length.spoken: Hur lång tid tar det till Göteborg?
trip-length.filled: Hur lång tid tar det till ⟦Göteborg⟧?

allergic.note: Add the food: nötter (NÖT-ter) nuts, jordnötter (YOORD-nöt-ter) peanuts, skaldjur (SKAAL-yür) shellfish. The audio uses nuts

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

recommend.note: At lunch, the dagens rätt, dish of the day, is the best value

beer.note: Shops sell only light beer; stronger drinks are sold at the state shop, Systembolaget

coffee.note: Fika, coffee with something sweet, is a daily ritual

water.note: Tap water is excellent and free

hot.note: Hot, and warm. Spicy is stark (stark)

cheers.note: Look each person in the eye, before and after you drink

bill.note: Service is included; rounding up is a nice extra

help.note: Shout it. For any emergency, call 112

need-doctor.note: For an ambulance, call 112. For medical advice, 1177
